chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: John Hammond, Teddy Wilson and Keg Johnson in Benny Carter's band
summary: Milt explains how Hammond recommended Teddy Wilson to Carter, and Wilson recommended Keg Johnson.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: You know, you're so very much right about the Benny Carter laboratory. I don't know whether it was official or not, but you must put John Hammond in there, who always liked Benny Carter, and he was the one who... Remember in 1932, he was the one that John Hammond recommended... He'd heard Teddy Wilson in Chicago, and told Benny Carter "Why don't you send for Teddy Wilson?" So Teddy Wilson came into New York to play with Benny Carter's band on the suggestion of John Hammond. And of course, when he got there, he'd been playing in Chicago with Keg Johnson and Budd Johnson and those fellows. And when Benny Carter was looking for a trombone player...

Teddy recommended Keg Johnson. They had all been living in the same house together, Miss Artis(?), in Chicago, see -- you know, old buddies -- and had been working on the same gig. So they sent for Keg Johnson. Now, Keg was my biggest friend. So my heart was broken because nobody had sent for me. You see? Then Keg Johnson gets in Benny Carter's band, as you say. And when you get in there, as Danny said, this is where everybody's looking. You're in the laboratory now. Anybody who is looking to get some musicians is looking to get it out of Benny Carter's band, because you've got to be pretty good to be in Benny
Carter's band, to play this music, and you'd be showing off at your best.
